# dumpyard — instructions for LLMs

A static site of pages, notes, PDFs and images. Any folder can sit behind its
own password; locking `/project-xyz/` covers everything under it.

Use the `dumpyard` CLI. Do not hand-edit generated files.

## Publish

```sh
dumpyard publish report.html                    # public, at /report/
dumpyard publish notes.md --space project-xyz   # into an existing folder
dumpyard publish ./project-xyz/ --set-password  # whole folder, one password
```

Each command commits, pushes and deploys. The URL is live in seconds.

## Passwords are retrievable — you do not need to remember them

```sh
dumpyard list                  # every lock, with its password
dumpyard password /project-xyz/   # just the password, for scripting
```

The CLI keeps every password it issues in `~/.config/dumpyard/passwords.json`
(mode 0600, outside the repo, never deployed). Read one back whenever you need
to re-share a link — republishing a locked folder prints its existing password
without changing it.

So: give the human the link and the password every time you publish or
republish something locked. Never tell them a password is unrecoverable.

## Remove

```sh
dumpyard remove /project-xyz/     # whole folder
dumpyard remove /project-xyz/notes  # one page
```

This deletes the content, drops the lock, forgets the password and deploys. The
content stays in git history, so it is recoverable; the live URL is not.

## What you write, what the build writes

You write: `.md`, self-contained `.html`, `.pdf`, images — into `public/`.
The build writes: every `index.html`, and `foo.html` for each `foo.md`.

Never edit `worker/locks.js`, `wrangler.jsonc`, any `index.html`, or a
`foo.html` that has a `foo.md` beside it. All are regenerated or load-bearing.

## Markdown

Obsidian-style links work and resolve at build time:

```
[[note]]           [[note|custom label]]        [[folder/note]]
![[diagram.png]]   ![[spec.pdf]]
```

A link that does not resolve renders as visible plain text and the build warns.
A public page cannot link into a locked folder — that link is dropped on
purpose, so a public index never leaks a locked title or URL. Fix warnings
rather than leaving them.

## Rules

- HTML pages are self-contained: inline CSS and JS, no frameworks, no external
  requests. Images and PDFs sit beside the page as normal files.
- Every markdown note starts with a `# Heading` — it becomes the title and the
  label other notes link it by.
- Folder names are lowercase kebab-case.
- Never put a password, token or key in the repo. Only salted hashes belong
  there, and only the CLI writes them.

## Handing over

A locked folder is deliberately absent from every public index, so the URL is
the only way in. When you finish, tell the human:

- the URL
- the password, if the folder is locked
- which parts are public and which are not
